svg.title: Amortized Analysis: Dynamic Array Doubling, Quarter-Shrink, and Binary Counter
svg.desc: Step-by-step animated visualization of dynamic array resizing with potential function Phi = 2S - C, quarter-shrink at C/4 vs C/2 thrashing, and binary counter increment bit-flips with potential Phi = popcount.
svg.text: Amortized Analysis: Dynamic Array Potential & Binary Counter Bit-Flips
Physicist's Method ĉ_i = c_i + Φ(D_i) - Φ(D_{i-1}) · Worst-case sequence guarantee without probability assumptions
1. Dynamic Array Doubling & Potential Φ(D) = 2S - C

g.text: Right after resize (half full): zero stored potential
Invariant: Φ(D) ≥ 0 holds because S ≥ C/2 after doubling
Cheap push (S=3, C=4): c_i = 1, ΔΦ = +2 ⇒ ĉ_i = 3
Accounting view: 1 pays insert, +2 banked on C & older sibling
Buffer full (S=4, C=4): Φ peaks at C = 4 credits ready!
Potential equals C=4: enough energy stored to copy all 4 items
ĉ_i = c_i + ΔΦ = (4 + 1) + (2 - 4) = 3 (Potential pays the copy spike!)

svg.text: Shrink C → C/2 only at S = C/4.

g.text: 3 trailing 1s → 0 released 3 credits; 1 zero → 1 banked 1 credit

svg.text: Each bit i flips ⌊n / 2^i⌋ times; total cost over n increments is strictly O(n).
Warning: Adding decrement() Breaks the Bound!
Alternating increment/decrement raises Φ by k-1 in one decrement (ĉ = 2t).
Amortization is a property of an OPERATION SET, not single ops!
